title: Session collation reporter and weighted quantile attributor
author: Anika Sharma
release_notes: Add session-collation reporter to the benchmark pipeline; expose cohort-weighted quantiles for session-attributed latency analysis. No public API changes.
description:
Motivation: our existing reporters produce per-request token-level metrics but lack a compact session-level collation useful for attributing long-tail latency to cohorts of tokens (primers, user messages, model responses). This PR introduces a session-collation reporter that groups requests into coherent sessions, emits a compact JSONL session artifact, and a weighted-quantile attributor that maps latency mass to token cohorts so we can answer questions like `which primer prefixes are responsible for p99 spikes?`.

What this changes: single PR that adds a new reporter (Python), a performant attributor (Go), a Rust-based normalization step for ingestion, dashboard assets, unit and integration tests, and CI bench assertions. Key deliverables: 1) src/reporters/session_collator.py — session grouping, KV-friendly checkpointing, streaming JSONL writer; 2) src/reporters/quantile_attributor.go — streamable weighted quantile attribution engine (bounded mem, single-pass); 3) ingest/pipeline/session_normalizer.rs — deterministic keying and timestamp bucketing for downstream TSDB; 4) dashboards/session-collation.json — Grafana panel config and example queries; 5) tests/* — unit and small-system integration harness with synthetic sessions.

Design notes: sessions are bounded by idle gaps (configurable, default 30s) and a max-token window to prevent unbounded aggregation for chatty clients. The attributor implements a cohort model (primer | user | assistant) and computes a weighted q-quantile attribution by allocating observed latency mass across cohorts proportional to token contribution and invocation phase. The algorithm is deterministic and numerically stable; it emits per-session cohort quantiles and an aggregate report that the dashboard consumes.

Compatibility: reporter is opt-in via benchmark config (reporters: ["session-collator"]). Outputs are backwards-compatible (JSONL lines include a legacy 'request_id' for crosswalks). There are no public API surface changes to the main serving runtime.

Checklist:

- [x] Unit tests added: python and go test suites
- [x] Integration test: small-system run with synthetic sessions reproducing known p99 pattern
- [x] Documentation: README + dashboard sample queries
- [x] Bench assertions: p95/p99 on a synthetic baseline to prevent regressions
- [x] CI green (build, unit, bench-smoke, lint)
